title: Where is it?
goal: Say where things are with prepositions of place, use du and des after de, and ask Où est… ? and Où sont… ?

items.fr: de + le = du, de + les = des
items.en: contractions of de with le and les (à côté du lit)

drills.en: The table is next to the sofa.
The chair is near the table.

drills.en: The cat is far from the chairs.

blocks.title: A busy morning in Ottawa
blocks.context: Nguyen is late for work. He can't find anything. His partner Mei helps.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.fr: Il est sur la table, dans la cuisine.
lines.en: It's on the table, in the kitchen.

lines.speaker: Nguyen
lines.fr: Non, il n'est pas sur la table.
lines.en: No, it's not on the table.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.fr: Alors, il est peut-être sous le canapé.
lines.en: Then maybe it's under the sofa.

lines.speaker: Nguyen
lines.fr: Ah oui, il est sous le canapé ! Et où sont mes clés ?
lines.en: Oh yes, it's under the sofa! And where are my keys?

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.fr: Tes clés ? Elles sont sur la chaise, à côté du lit.
lines.en: Your keys? They're on the chair, next to the bed.

lines.speaker: Nguyen
lines.fr: Merci ! Et le chat ? Où est le chat ?
lines.en: Thanks! And the cat? Where's the cat?

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.fr: Le chat ? Il est derrière toi !

blocks.body: New words to understand here: [[les clés]] (keys), [[le chat]] (the cat), [[peut-être]] (maybe). Notice that the phone is [[il]] and the keys are [[elles]]: French uses il/elle for things too, following the noun's gender.

blocks.title: Où est… ? Où sont… ?
blocks.body:
To ask where something is, use [[où]] (where) + [[être]]:

- one thing: [[Où est le chat ?]]
- more than one: [[Où sont mes clés ?]]

In everyday speech you also hear the question word at the end: [[Le chat est où ?]] Both are correct.

In the answer, replace the thing with [[il]] / [[elle]] / [[ils]] / [[elles]]: [[Il est sous le lit.]] [[Elles sont sur la chaise.]]

blocks.title: De + the article
head: de + …
becomes
example
blocks.note: Only **le** and **les** combine with [[de]]. [[De le]] and [[de les]] never appear in French. With a city or a name there is no article: [[loin de Montréal]], [[à côté de Karim]].

blocks.title: Where is it?
blocks.note: When nothing follows, drop the [[de]]: [[La salle de bains est à côté.]] (The bathroom is right nearby.) [[C'est loin ?]] (Is it far?)

examples.fr: Le téléphone est sur la table.
examples.en: The phone is on the table.

examples.fr: Les chaises sont devant le canapé.
examples.en: The chairs are in front of the sofa.

examples.fr: La cuisine est en face du salon.
examples.en: The kitchen is opposite the living room.

examples.fr: Mes parents habitent loin de Montréal.
examples.en: My parents live far from Montréal.

blocks.title: Du and des again?
blocks.body:
You already know [[du]] and [[des]] from food: [[du pain]] (some bread). Here they are **the same contraction** of [[de + le]] and [[de + les]], but here [[de]] is part of the preposition ([[à côté de]], [[près de]]) and does not mean *some*.

- [[Je mange du pain.]] = I eat some bread.
- [[Le pain est à côté du fromage.]] = The bread is next to the cheese.

The form is the same; the meaning comes from the words around it.

examples.fr: La table est à côté du canapé.
examples.en: The table is next to the sofa.

blocks.body:
- **Sur vs sous:** [[sur]] (on) has the tight French *u*; [[sous]] (under) has *ou* like “soo”. Mixing them up puts your phone on the bed instead of under it!
- **Forgetting de:** say [[à côté de la cuisine]], not [[à côté la cuisine]]. But [[sur]], [[sous]], [[devant]], [[derrière]], [[entre]] take no [[de]]: [[devant la table]].
- **De le:** always [[du]]: [[près du salon]].
- **With or without de:** [[La cuisine est à gauche du salon.]] (to the left of the living room) but [[La cuisine est à gauche.]] (on the left) when nothing follows.

In everyday Québec French you will often hear [[en arrière de]] for [[derrière]] and [[en avant de]] for [[devant]]: [[Le chat est en arrière du divan.]] It's informal; understand it, but use [[derrière]] and [[devant]] when you write or speak in a formal situation.

examples.fr: Le stationnement est en arrière de la maison.
examples.en: The parking lot is behind the house.

blocks.title: Listen and repeat
blocks.note: Repeat each line out loud. Pay special attention to [[sur]] and [[sous]].

lines.tip: Say “ee” with your lips rounded for the u.
Two r sounds, one in the middle and one at the end: “dair-yair”, with the French r from the throat.
[[où]] sounds like “oo”; the s of [[mes]] and [[clés]] is silent.

blocks.prompt: Look around the room you're in. Describe where four things are, using at least four different prepositions.
checklist: Four objects or pieces of furniture
At least one preposition with de (à côté de, en face de…)

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Je suis dans le salon. Le canapé est devant la table. Mon téléphone est sur le canapé. Les chaises sont à côté de la table, et le chat est sous une chaise. La cuisine est en face du salon.
models.en: I'm in the living room. The sofa is in front of the table. My phone is on the sofa. The chairs are next to the table, and the cat is under a chair. The kitchen is opposite the living room.

blocks.prompt: A friend is staying at your place while you're away. Write a note telling them where three or four things are (rooms, furniture, keys…).
checklist: At least three things and where they are
Use du or des at least once
Use où or a question if you like

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Salut Sofia ! Bienvenue ! Les clés sont sur la table, dans la cuisine. Ta chambre est à côté de la salle de bains. Les toilettes sont en face du salon. Le chat est souvent sous le lit. Bonne semaine ! Karim
models.en: Hi Sofia! Welcome! The keys are on the table, in the kitchen. Your bedroom is next to the bathroom. The toilet is opposite the living room. The cat is often under the bed. Have a good week! Karim

summary:
- Say where things are with [[sur, sous, devant, derrière, entre, à côté de, en face de, près de, loin de, à gauche de, à droite de]]
- Contract [[de + le = du]] and [[de + les = des]]: [[à côté du lit]]
- Ask [[Où est… ?]] and [[Où sont… ?]]
